### Historical audit — S0290

**Scope:** Visible chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations below refer to S0290, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0016/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Neither the reference nor rendered images are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Goal: line 1, `model_request` | Reconstruct a single indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion. The student’s inventory interprets it as a woodworking shop; that interpretation is not independent image verification (line 3, `model_response`). |
| Initial scene: lines 3–4, H response and step-1 `execute` | Code creates multiple named assets: two benches, saw, drill press, CNC router, lamp, lumber rack, stove, storage and architecture. Named child meshes include legs, vise, gantry and handles; hierarchy does not establish physical connection. Splayed legs are rotated. Colors and geometric log-end disks approximate surfaces; no external texture is used. Camera, world and four area lights are configured. |
| First validation: lines 6–11 | Build and render completed with return code 0; `execution_result` reports `ok: true` and a saved image, and step 1 was selected. The next H request included that image and asked for comparison. This validates execution, not resemblance. |
| Autonomous correction: lines 13–20 | H reports that the first scene was too small, viewed from the opposite end, and exposed room boundaries. It executes a complete revision: camera moves to the other side with a longer lens, floor and wall expand, bench depth and panel details change, and lighting is reduced. Step 2 builds and renders successfully and is selected. These discrepancies are H’s judgments, not independently verified findings. |
| Further correction: lines 21–28 | Given the second render, H reports the bench and tools still too small, excessive floor, and pale background. Step 3 moves the camera closer and left, darkens background colors and reduces lighting. Its build and render each complete with return code 0; the visible chunk ends before an execution-result or selection event for this step. |
| Input and exploration: lines 1–2, 11–12, 21–22 | The system supplies general inventory, cost and comparison instructions; the runner supplies render feedback. No separate teacher diagnosis or proposed update is visible, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be claimed. The student independently makes two render-informed revisions; session records show no auxiliary tool calls. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Three builds and renders technically completed; final submission and formal task success are **unknown** in the visible chunk. There is no visible technical interruption or empty patch. The code demonstrates multiple objects, color assignments, intended part hierarchy, object pose, and camera/light changes, but not correct geometry, actual part contact, texture fidelity, framing, illumination, or image completeness. Whether either camera diagnosis was correct, and whether the third render improved the match, remain unresolved. A transferable observation is the distinction between successful rendering and verified reconstruction; the particular bench dimensions, camera moves and darkening are task-specific choices, not validated general rules.
